column5: F: Where does this come from? | M: A building model.
column6: F: Where does all this come from? | M: From a building model. Its quantities were priced and pushed into the ERP as one project order. Here it is, just over seven million dollars.

column5: F: In how many parts? | M: Eight phases.
column6: F: And in how many parts? | M: Eight phases. The outlined column adds up to the same seven million, to the cent. Now, how does a boss see this?

column4: §FILM_DASH_SHOT d0_glance total_projects=3 active_projects=3 approved_budget=100:7063922.98 actual_cost=100:5367.00 forecast_cost=100:7459.45 health green=0 amber=1 red=0 none=2
column5: F: And this is the dashboard? | M: One screen.
column6: F: And this is the dashboard? | M: One screen. Three projects, all active. Planned, just over seven million dollars. Spent so far, about five thousand. One project is amber, two have nothing due yet. The forecast carries a warning, because spending and progress are not on the same basis yet.

column5: F: Can I see which projects? | M: Click the number.
column6: F: Can I see which projects make that number? | M: Click it. A panel opens with the three projects. The big one is the order we just saw, the same seven million.

column5: F: Why is it amber? | M: Click amber.
column6: F: And why is it amber? | M: Click amber. One project, the order. A phase is past its end date and is not ticked complete, so it cannot be green, and the schedule says delayed. The budget is fine.

column5: F: And the money spent? | M: Same way.
column6: F: And the money spent? | M: The same way. Three rows, and only the order has spent anything so far.

column5: F: How is it calculated? | M: One click.
column6: F: And how is each number calculated? | M: One more click. The formula opens under the tile, in plain database columns, so anyone can check it.

column5: F: What is Projects? | M: Every project.
column6: F: What is the Projects entry? | M: Every project, with planned, actual and committed money, and a link to its model.

column5: F: And Budget and Cost? | M: The money.
column6: F: And Budget and Cost? | M: The money per project: planned, committed, invoiced and actual, each in the project's own currency.

column5: F: Procurement Risks? | M: Where buying may go wrong.
column6: F: What are Procurement Risks? | M: Where buying may go wrong: open orders, projects over-committed, budget with nothing ordered. Today one project has no order. These are proposed.

column5: F: Approval Pending? | M: Waiting for someone.
column6: F: And Approval Pending? | M: Workflow approvals waiting for someone to act. Ten now, the same as the red badge.

column5: F: And Handover? | M: How close to done.
column6: F: And Handover? | M: How close projects are to handover: every phase complete, or closed. None yet, and no drawing register on this server. Also proposed.

column5: F: Which systems does it run on? | M: Two.
column6: F: Which systems does it run on? | M: Two. Every number is a row in iDempiere's own Performance Analysis tables: what to count, the query, the target. On the Kernel ERP the rows load as data; on legacy iDempiere, as plain SQL scripts.

column6: F: Is it really the same on both? | M: We checked. Eighty-nine values compared between the two systems and the page, none differ. And fifty-nine click-through checks, none failed. The test server is local, and the rates are examples.
